# Lit Agent Keychain

> Owner-authorized, locally encrypted credentials for AI agents. Each secret is encrypted in the owner's browser to its own immutable Lit Action, whose key is derived inside an Intel TDX enclave on the Lit Protocol network. An agent holds a local Ed25519 identity; the owner approves its public key per secret with an expiry (default 30 days, max 90). The action verifies the owner's signed receipt and the agent's signature on every request, then returns the value encrypted to that agent only. The Keychain service stores ciphertext and signed policies; it cannot forge approvals or read secrets.

Key facts for agents:

- Install: `npm install @lit-protocol/keychain@2.0.4` (Node 22+). CLI binary: `keychain`.
- Generate an identity locally: `npx @lit-protocol/keychain@2.0.4 init ./agent-identity.json`. Share ONLY `publicKey` with the owner.
- The owner approves that public key in the web app and downloads an agent config (`*.keychain.json`) containing public locators plus a scoped Chipotle execution key. The execution key pays for Lit execution; it cannot read a secret by itself.
- Read at runtime: `new Keychain(identity.privateKey, config).get("NAME")`, or `npx @lit-protocol/keychain@2.0.4 get ./agent-identity.json ./NAME.keychain.json NAME`. For "use inside Lit" secrets: `.use("NAME", input)` or `npx @lit-protocol/keychain@2.0.4 use ./agent-identity.json ./NAME.keychain.json NAME '{...}'`.
- Hand a secret to one command without printing it: `npx @lit-protocol/keychain@2.0.4 run ./agent-identity.json ./NAME.keychain.json -- <command>` puts each export-release secret in the command's environment under its own name, prints nothing, and exits with the command's status. `--only A,B` selects secrets, `--env SECRET=ENV_VAR` renames one, `--file SECRET=PATH` writes one to a new mode-0600 file that is removed when the command exits (for tools that read credentials from a path). Prefer `run` over `get` whenever the value is only needed by a tool, to avoid CLI printing. A child can still log or disclose plaintext; this is not a sandbox. SIGKILL can leave --file plaintext behind; unlink does not guarantee erasure.
- MCP (local stdio, never hosted): `claude mcp add lit-keychain -- npx -y @lit-protocol/keychain@2.0.4 mcp /absolute/path/agent-identity.json /absolute/path/NAME.keychain.json`. Tools: `list_secrets`, `get_secret`, one tool per catalog action (`stripe_balance`, `openai_chat`, `github_read_file`, `slack_post_message`, `supabase_tables`), `list_actions`, `agent_public_key`. `npx @lit-protocol/keychain@2.0.4 actions` prints the current catalog.
- Actions: `export` delivers the plaintext encrypted to the agent. Every other action uses the credential only inside the enclave for one fixed upstream call and returns a bounded result (Stripe balance, OpenAI chat completion, GitHub file read, Slack post message, Supabase table reads and inserts under an owner allowlist); the credential is not returned to the agent (the provider receives it over TLS) and the action can reach only the hosts its manifest declares. The catalog lives in its own public repository and is open to contributions: https://github.com/LIT-Protocol/agent-keychain-library
- The SDK attests the Lit endpoint (TDX quote, RTMR replay, on-chain whitelist on Base, TLS binding in Node) before execution requests to configured/pinned production origins and fails closed on check failure. Unknown origins are not automatically attested; independently verify config.litApiUrl and explicitly pin custom deployments. The on-chain step rotates through public Base RPCs; set `KEYCHAIN_BASE_RPC_URL` to pin your own. Never disable attestation outside local development.
- Errors: the enclave answers every refusal with a bare access denial, so the client explains what it can see. `Access denied: the owner disabled this secret`, `... permission expired`, `... agent <key> is not approved`, and `... approved for version N, not the current version` are policy problems for the owner to fix in Keychain. For a connected service, `Access denied: Lit ran the <action> ... did not complete` is an unclassified failure after local policy checks: input/credential mismatch, provider error, timeout or size/schema limits are possible; have the owner check privately. Do not blindly retry writes. `Attestation: no Base RPC endpoint answered` is a transient RPC outage or rate limit: retry, or set `KEYCHAIN_BASE_RPC_URL`.
- There are no setup tokens, management bearer tokens, or server-minted grants. Never ask the owner for a private key or Google token.
